documentedMappings: POST /files: raw octet-stream; response uuid, sha256, size (-1 unknown).
POST /instances: pinned image UUID, command/args, files, disabled networking, timeout, disposable state, writable-layer cap.
GET /operations/{operationId}: status and metadata.result streams/state; consumed_cpu is CPU seconds or null.
DELETE /operations/{operationId}: 202 accepts cancellation; poll for terminal state.
unresolved: No current verified account, image UUID/content binding, entitlement, rates or controls receipt.
Public instance schema does not expose memory, PID, CPU-quota, read-only-rootfs, capability-drop or no-new-privileges flags; verified equivalent external controls are mandatory.
No documented file-delete endpoint in the index; upload retention and its billing need account evidence.
Result resource cost has no documented currency; measuredCostUsd remains null.
No client-supplied creation UUID/idempotency field documented; a lost POST response can leave an operation without a known UUID.
GET status schema uses uppercase states; some examples elsewhere show lowercase. Strict adapter uses the schema and requires account conformance verification.
Publication/update dates were not supplied by these fetched pages; fetchedAt is an inspection timestamp only.
limitations: Reference records are trusted control-plane inputs, not self-authenticating proofs. No receipt was created for real execution.
Transport and runner tests are synthetic and do not prove service entitlement, containment, cancellation, billing or latency.
Live startup, durable budget reservations and crash recovery are not wired. Request intent records preserve ambiguity but cannot cancel an unknown operation ID.
